title: Crushing the Serpent Under the Heel

feed.text: Says the Croix-des-Bouquets plain is under heavy fire; about 100 Salvadoran elite troops are sweeping Santo, Marassa, Shada and Croix-des-Bouquets with Haitian police (PNH) and GSF armored vehicles; hospitals are overwhelmed with wounded gang members; gunmen tried to seize doctors in Santo 22 and Sainte Camille; and Dominican President Abinader ordered the border closed completely.
feed.evidence: photo; no named source; long text post
feed.other: The Dominican Defense Ministry said on 22 and 23 Oct that it ruled out closing the border (El Día, n.com.do) and again on 24 Oct (Infobae). Those reports predate this post, so they are not an answer to it, but they are the only Dominican statements found.

feed.who: Cartel Watch (@CartelWatchNet), a self-described privately funded NGO
feed.text: Says intense clashes are under way between Salvadoran special forces and armed gangs as part of a rescue operation authorized by Bukele.
feed.evidence: video, 87 seconds; no named source. What the video shows: two phone clips joined together. Night: a shaky view of a dirt street between unfinished cinderblock walls, a parked white pickup, blurry figures, loud automatic gunfire and shouting. Day: filmed from inside a room through a metal door at a dirt yard with a wheelbarrow, distant gunfire, a man speaking what sounds like Haitian Creole. No uniforms, flags or aircraft are visible, and the video shows no date or place.

feed.who: Eduardo Menoni (@eduardomenoni), Venezuelan journalist and analyst
feed.text: Says armored vehicles of the anti-gang force arrived at Las Américas International Airport in the Dominican Republic, to be moved to Port-au-Prince as reinforcements for the search for the four technicians.
feed.evidence: video, 39 seconds (not yet watched by us); no named source

feed.text: Posts three photos of Salvadoran armored and tactical Yagu vehicles (Mexican-made, as the post says) being loaded onto a US C-130J at the international airport at Comalapa, El Salvador, to fight 400 Mawozo and Chen Mechan in the search for the four technicians.
feed.evidence: 3 photos; no named source

feed.text: Says sources on the ground report the gangs collapsing as Salvadoran special forces arrive: the Chen Mechan base was destroyed completely after drone attacks and heavy fire, and its faction no longer exists in the area; Lanmò San Jou's group suffered mass losses and its improvised medical shelters are overwhelmed.
feed.evidence: 2 photos; sources unnamed; not yet reported by others

feed.text: Says Salvadoran forces are clashing with gangs in Haiti during an intense search and rescue operation for four kidnapped aviation technicians. An earlier version at 03:10 (post 2113785100605264057) said "four kidnapped soldiers."
feed.evidence: video, 85 seconds (not yet watched by us); no named source

feed.text: Says Salvadoran military forces are already in Haiti after Bukele announced a rescue operation to free four air force technicians.
feed.evidence: video, 16 seconds (not yet watched by us)

feed.who: Héctor Rodríguez Pimentel (@HectorRPimentel), former Dominican senator and journalist
feed.text: Says Bukele reached Washington on the night of 22 Oct for an urgent meeting with Trump (citing AP), that 100 Salvadoran special forces landed in Port-au-Prince on 22 Oct and 100 more were due that night for 200 in total, that the Salvadoran law changed the mission from medical evacuation to deploying civilian and military personnel, and that Bukele is asking Trump for satellite intelligence and drones over Croix-des-Bouquets, armed helicopters, and UN permission for the GSF to use offensive lethal force. Quotes Trump on Truth Social: "I look forward to seeing President Bukele of El Salvador on Monday."
feed.evidence: video, 49 seconds (not yet watched by us); cites AP and the GSF; no named source for the requests Bukele is said to make
feed.other: The Salvadoran law date: Pimentel says 10 Oct; Diario El Mundo (El Salvador) reports it approved 29 Sep, published 30 Sep, in force 2 Oct 2026.

feed.who: Nayib Bukele, President of El Salvador (@nayibbukele)
feed.text: Quotes Humberto Salazar's post and answers critics who say Haiti's gangs are different from El Salvador's and that this will be Bukele's Waterloo. Says everyone who enlisted is a believer, calls the Haitian gangs "satanic" and says it is public knowledge that they make human sacrifices, and says God will grant victory (Deuteronomy 28:7). Gives no troop number in the part we could read.
feed.evidence: on the record, signed post

feed.text: Says Bukele "starts the war": 3,000 soldiers "armed to the teeth" arrived in Haiti with Haitian military forces to rescue four soldiers.
feed.evidence: video, 6 minutes (posted via another account, @DefenceReviewGr); no named source
feed.other: The Haitian Times (23 Oct) reports about 100 special forces; Le Nouvelliste (23 Oct) cites an unnamed source for 450; El País (24 Oct) reports six planes and about 100 elite troops.

feed.text: Says El Salvador announced sending a contingent of 3,000 troops, says the four are probably dead, and names Claude Celestin (Chen Mechan) and Wilson Joseph, Lanmò San Jou (400 Mawozo), as the leaders of the groups that hold the area. Asks whether Haiti will be "Bukele's Waterloo." Bukele quoted this post in his reply at 20:59.
feed.evidence: 2 photos; says "according to the international press"; no named source
feed.other: We did not find a 3,000 figure in any Bukele post we read.

feed.text: Reports 450 Salvadoran soldiers are in Port-au-Prince on Friday 23 Oct, with the mission of searching for the four missing and reinforcing the Gang Suppression Force. Quotes a source: "Another plane just arrived tonight with 100 soldiers on board. We are at 450 Salvadorans." Says it knows of no American soldiers there.
feed.evidence: anonymous source ("a well-informed source")
feed.other: Listín Diario (Dominican Republic) headlined on 24 Oct that the total reached 450. The Haitian Times reported about 100 special forces arriving.

feed.text: Reports a Salvadoran contingent of 100 special forces arrived to help search; residents near the ambush area said they could still hear gunfire on Wednesday evening and some had fled; quotes ACLED analyst María Fernanda Arocha: "Haiti's gangs have escalated their violence as they are increasingly willing and able to confront international forces directly." Quotes Bukele: "Our mission consists only of pilots and technical personnel whose primary task is to carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war." Names the force commander as Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri.
feed.evidence: named reporters and named analyst; residents quoted

feed.where: Turkish wire service and a Florida daily
feed.text: Anadolu reports that Wilson Joseph, called Lanmò San Jou, leader of 400 Mawozo, posted a video showing large quantities of ammunition and challenged Bukele, saying he would not flee and was ready to fight Salvadoran forces. A Haiti analyst quoted by the Miami Herald says the Viv Ansanm coalition had been fragmenting and that this incident may restore cohesion; "Krisla and Lanmò San Jou have spoken this week." No gang has publicly claimed the abduction.
feed.evidence: video of Lanmò San Jou circulated on social media (not yet watched by us); analyst quoted without being named in the part we read

feed.text: Says Bukele is sending Defense Minister René Merino Monroy to Haiti with 3,000 "patriotic Salvadoran soldiers" to fight the gangs, with "total support" from the Dominican Republic.
feed.evidence: photo; no named source

feed.who: Haitian National Police (PNH), reported by Diario El Mundo (El Salvador) from EFE
feed.text: The PNH says an offensive began on Sunday in the Cul-de-Sac plain with special forces, in Croix-des-Missions, Santo, Carrefour Marassa and the Dyo and Las Vegas corridors, to remove illegal checkpoints and retake gang territory, and that numerous gang members died, including local leaders. Haitian paper Métronome reported 300 Salvadoran soldiers might arrive on Thursday, with no official confirmation.
feed.evidence: on-record police statement; no count of dead given

feed.text: Addresses the gang chiefs and members holding the four: they are aviation technicians, not combatants; they were seized "cowardly" while returning from buying food at a market; "today we launched a military operation to rescue them"; "today's attack is nothing compared to what is coming if you do not hand over all four hostages alive"; "we have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too."
feed.evidence: on the record, signed post; video, 60 seconds (not yet watched by us)

feed.text: Reports an account he says Jimmy "Barbecue" Chérizier, spokesman of Viv Ansanm, gave him: five GSF members were ambushed at a supermarket in Santo on 18 Oct by Chen Mechan fighters, their armored Land Cruiser was set on fire, all five died, and the gang is holding the bodies. The article's own title uses the word "mercenaries" for them. Says the New York Times reported five Salvadoran soldiers missing citing "three people familiar with the situation," while the Salvadoran military says four. Says the GSF is at 28 percent of capacity.
feed.evidence: one named gang leader's account as relayed by the author; not yet reported by others; no photo or video given
feed.other: Salvadoran military and AP: four aviation technicians fled the burning vehicle and are unaccounted for. Ambassador Waltz told the UN Security Council on 19 Oct that attackers fired hundreds of rounds and used explosives and that authorities believe all four survived.

feed.who: Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, speaking at the Security Council; reported by EFE via France 24
feed.text: Said the four Salvadorans disappeared on Sunday 18 Oct when armed gangs attacked their armored vehicle as they returned to base from a market on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, that attackers fired hundreds of rounds and used explosives, and that authorities believe all four survived. On X the US mission to the UN told gang bosses: "The Gang Suppression Force is coming for you."
feed.evidence: on the record, named official
links: US mission to the UN on X, 19 Oct

feed.text: UN officials told the Security Council that between July and September over 1,000 people were killed and over 100 abducted in Haiti, and described the Gang Suppression Force as severely understrength.
feed.evidence: on the record, UN document

salvador: Four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with the Gang Suppression Force went missing on 18 Oct 2026 after their armored vehicle was attacked in Santo, Croix-des-Bouquets (Haitian Times; Salvadoran military via AP). Bukele says they are medical-evacuation personnel, not combatants.
On 21 Oct Bukele announced a military operation to rescue them and warned the gangs in Haitian Creole that he could "finish" them as he did in El Salvador.

Troop numbers differ by source: about 100 special forces (Haitian Times, 23 Oct; El País, 24 Oct), 200 (Pimentel, 23 Oct, quoting the GSF), 450 (Le Nouvelliste's anonymous source, 23 Oct, and a Listín Diario headline, 24 Oct), 3,000 (Salazar, Ciprian Reyes, Noticiero-502gt). Bukele's own posts that we read give no number.

Law: El Salvador's Special Transitory Law for the participation of its armed forces in the Gang Suppression Force was approved 29 Sep, published 30 Sep, in force 2 Oct 2026, and authorizes participation until Oct 2027 (Diario El Mundo, El Salvador).

Equipment: Armapedia's photos show Yagu armored vehicles loaded onto a US C-130J at Comalapa; Menoni's video is said to show armored vehicles arriving at Las Américas airport in the Dominican Republic.
gsf: The Gang Suppression Force (GSF) is the UN-authorized force under Security Council resolution 2793 (2025). Its mandate was renewed in September 2026 for six months, through March 2027 (Haitian Times).

Its commander is Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri (Haitian Times). Contributing countries named by Haïti Liberté: Chad, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mongolia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The UN calls it severely understrength; EFE says it has about 2,000 of a planned 5,500 from six countries.
In July a GSF patrol in Tabarre came under fire near an illegal checkpoint in Kraze Baryè territory; the GSF said three armed men were killed (Haitian Times, 19 Oct).
haitian: The Haitian National Police say an offensive began 18 Oct in the Cul-de-Sac plain, in Croix-des-Missions, Santo, Carrefour Marassa and the Dyo and Las Vegas corridors, with many gang members killed and no count given (EFE via Diario El Mundo).
Haiti's government has called the soldiers' release a priority and says it is coordinating with the GSF (Haitian Times).
Haiti's government postponed the elections planned for December indefinitely in early October (EFE via France 24).
us: Ambassador Mike Waltz briefed the UN Security Council on 19 Oct and the US mission publicly told gang bosses the GSF "is coming for you."

Pimentel says Bukele was in Washington on 22 to 23 Oct to meet Trump and is asking for satellite intelligence, drones, armed helicopters and UN permission for offensive force. We have not found an official readout; the White House gallery page for a Trump-Bukele meeting that we opened is dated July 2025.
The US designated Viv Ansanm and Gran Grif as terrorist organizations on 2 May 2025 (State Department).
contractors: Haiti's government created a Task Force that uses armed drones and helicopters against gangs and is supported by private contractors from Vectus Global, the company of Erik Prince (AP and Human Rights Watch).

Human Rights Watch (10 Mar 2026): Haitian security forces and private contractors working with them carried out drone strikes; at least 1,243 people were killed in 141 operations between 1 Mar 2025 and 21 Jan 2026, including at least 43 adults reportedly not gang members and 17 children; 738 were injured.

Vectus Global's contract was reportedly extended by one year at an additional $52 million, with operations expanded into Bas-Artibonite (Le Placentin, 10 Oct 2026, and other reports; we have not seen the contract). Reuters reported in Aug 2025 that Prince planned to keep personnel in Haiti for 10 years; OPB reported nearly 200 personnel.
Haïti Liberté (Kim Ives) uses the word "mercenaries" for GSF members; that is the author's word, not ours.

gangs: The coalition of the main Port-au-Prince gangs, formed in 2024 per El País (one source dates it September 2023). Jimmy "Barbecue" Chérizier is a leading figure and its spokesman. Designated a terrorist organization by the US on 2 May 2025. The Miami Herald's analyst says it had been fragmenting, and that this incident may restore its cohesion.
Led by Wilson Joseph, "Lanmò San Jou," operating in Croix-des-Bouquets and part of Viv Ansanm. He posted a video of ammunition and challenged Bukele (Anadolu).

Part of Viv Ansanm. Haïti Liberté, relaying Chérizier, says its fighters ambushed the GSF members in Santo. Salazar names Claude Celestin as its head. Martínez says its base was destroyed (not yet reported by others).
Controls territory in Tabarre where a GSF patrol came under fire in July (Haitian Times).
Gran Grif, Kokorat San Ras and Canaan

From March 2026 they attacked dozens of localities in the lower Artibonite; Gran Grif was designated a terrorist group by the US with Viv Ansanm (UN Panel of Experts report, hosted on HaitiDocs, and State Department).
Named by the Miami Herald's analyst as one of two leaders who spoke publicly this week.
numbers: about 100 (Haitian Times, El País) / 200 (Pimentel) / 450 (Le Nouvelliste source, Listín Diario) / 3,000 (Salazar, Reyes, Noticiero-502gt)
four (Salvadoran military, AP, Waltz); five (New York Times, as quoted by Haïti Liberté)
Killed in Haiti, Jul to Sep 2026
Fighting in Cité Soleil and Cul-de-Sac, 6 Mar to 31 Jul 2026
613 killed, 214 of them not tied to gangs (UN Panel of Experts report)
Drone strikes by Haitian forces and contractors, Mar 2025 to Jan 2026
